name: Executive order of January 4, 1883 setting apart the Hualapai (Walapai) reservation
promises: Not a treaty: a presidential order. It set apart for the Hualapai a reserve beginning on the Colorado River five miles east of Tinnakah Spring and running by Music Mountains back to the river, at least 2 miles south of Peach Spring and 2 miles east of Pine Spring (Royce p. 910; Commission finding 16).

Royce notes General Willcox had set the tract apart as a military reservation on July 8, 1881 and the Commissioner of Indian Affairs recommended it become an Indian reserve on September 5, 1882 (Royce p. 911).

breaches.what: The Commission found that the Hualapai's Indian title to their aboriginal land outside this reservation was extinguished by the United States on January 4, 1883, when this order set the reservation aside and the tribe accepted it, and that it was extinguished without payment of compensation.

landTaken: The Hualapai aboriginal land outside the reservation: "Excluding petitioner's reservation", 4,459,500 acres (finding 20, December 21, 1966).
compensation: $2,950,000 by stipulated final judgment of June 18, 1968 (Dockets 90 and 122), a compromise. The Commission had valued the land at $2,800,000 as of January 4, 1883.
today: In United States v. Santa Fe Pacific Railroad Co. (December 8, 1941) the Supreme Court held that the creation of this reservation at the Walapai's request and their acceptance of it amounted to a relinquishment of their claims to land outside it, while rejecting the railroad's argument that earlier events had extinguished their title. That ruling went against the tribe on the outside lands and is not counted as a breach; the Commission later held the United States liable for their value.

nationVoice.summary: The Tribe says an executive order established the Hualapai reservation in 1883, and that the reservation covers about one million acres along 108 miles of the Grand Canyon and the Colorado River.

Audit 2026-11-08: the 4,459,500 acres were described as the whole Hualapai aboriginal holding (and plain said the order took "the rest" of a 4,459,500-acre homeland). Finding 20 (17 Ind. Cl. Comm. 456) says "Excluding petitioner's reservation, the tract ... consists of 4,459,500 acres": the figure is the land taken, outside the reservation. Corrected in the breach, landTaken and plain; finding 20 added as a source. The same wording is in cession-1886-10-01-walapai (not in this audit sample).

plain.promised: Not a treaty. An 1883 presidential order set apart a reservation along the Colorado River for the Hualapai, at the tribe's request.
plain.happened: The Indian Claims Commission found that with this order the United States took 4,459,500 acres of Hualapai homeland outside the reservation without paying for it.
plain.today: The Commission valued the land at $2,800,000; the claims were settled for $2,950,000 in 1968.
